title: Compact Evidence Serializer and Audit Index PRD (raw)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This note captures a pragmatic proposal for a compact evidence serializer and a lightweight audit index that sits between our approval-gates and the customer-managed networking handover flow. Goal: produce small, privacy-minimizing, forensically-useful artifacts for every customer VPC change event that both Redwood and the customer can store/search and (if needed) submit to downstream forensics. This is a working draft — design questions and tradeoffs are explicit.

Why we need a serializer + index:
- Current audit payloads are large, free-form, and differ by operator; makes storage, transfer, and quick triage expensive.
- For private deployments we must: minimize data leakage, provide immutable proofs, and keep the retention surface small to satisfy enterprise legal/compliance constraints.
- A compact canonical representation enables sampling, fast binary diffs, and efficient integrity verification (signatures + digest chaining).

High-level design principles:
1) Deterministic, canonical encoding: choose a stable field order and canonical JSON-like layout (or concise binary CBOR) so signature verification is robust across stacks.
2) Minimalism: include only the fields required for triage and reconstruction; external pointers allowed for large blobs (pcap, full configs) stored in customer-owned buckets.
3) Cryptographic linkage: include digest of prior evidence (lightweight chain) per customer-resource to detect missing events.
4) Dual-signature model: Redwood signs serializer output; if customer KMS is available, include customer signature to prove handover acknowledgement.
5) Indexable tokens: surface a small set of searchable tokens (resource-id, change-type, operator-id, decision-gate-id, timestamp-range bin) for low-latency lookups.
6) Privacy/PII minimization: redact IP payloads beyond prefix-level; persist only hashes for sensitive attachments unless explicitly permitted.

Proposed evidence record (human-readable sketch):
- evidence_id: stable UUID v4 as primary id
- resource_key: "customer:<org-id>:vpc:<vpc-id>:subnet:<subnet-id>" (string)
- seq: integer (per resource monotonic counter)
- timestamp: ISO-8601 UTC
- change_type: e.g., "route-add", "sg-update", "peering-create"
- gate_decision: {"gate_id": "appr-gk-7", "decision": "approved", "actor": "ops@example.com"} (note: in canonical form, flatten gate_id decision actor to compact tokens)
- summary_hash: SHA256 of normalized diff payload (stored separately)
- minimal_snapshot: base64(CBOR) of a delta object (max 2KB) - contains only changed keys and values
- attachments: [ {"kind":"full-config","url":"s3://cust-bucket/...","digest":"sha256:...","size": 23456} ]
- prior_digest: sha256 of prior evidence canonical bytes (or null)
- signatures: ["redwood:siG...","customer:kms:siG..."]
- retention_class: enum("ephemeral-30d","standard-1y","legal-hold")
- routing_index: ["org:acme","vpc:12345","change:route-add","actor:r.miller"]

Important tradeoffs discussed:
- JSON vs CBOR vs custom binary: JSON is debuggable but verbose. CBOR strikes a balance, but requires libraries in partner stacks. We propose canonical-CBOR as the on-wire and on-disk format, with an optional compact-JSON for UI debug views.
- Where to store full payloads: prefer customer-owned object storage (S3/GCS/Azure) with a signed, time-limited URL or cross-account replication. Redwood retains compact evidence and hashes only. This reduces our egress/retention obligations and aligns with privacy.
- Signing model: Redwood will sign every serialized evidence object using a service signing key stored in our KMS. If customer-managed KMS exists, we include their signature in the same record. For customers without KMS, a Redwood-signed receipt plus operator acknowledgement is acceptable.

Index design and query patterns:
- Primary index: evidence_id -> canonical bytes metadata (small: <1KB) stored in Dynamo/Spanner with TTL based on retention_class.
- Secondary inverted tokens: token -> list(evidence_id) (sharded by org) for quick discovery. Tokens limited to 5 per event to keep index size bounded.
- Time-binning: for rapid range queries index also stores day-bucket tags (YYYY-MM-DD).

Privacy and legal considerations:
- Default retention for compact evidence: 90 days (ephemeral) unless customer selects longer.
- Sensitive fields (full IP addresses, internal hostnames) must be redacted or stored as one-way hashes; plaintext only in customer-owned attachments.
- Provide a legal-hold API to flip retention_class to legal-hold and export full artifacts when required.

Operational flow (sketch):
1) Operator initiates change via Console/CLI -> request enters approval-gate service.
2) Gate evaluates rules, emits gate_decision record.
3) Change executor generates normalized diff and minimal_snapshot.
4) Compact serializer composes canonical record, computes digest chain, signs with Redwood KMS.
5) Record stored in Redwood compact store; large artifacts uploaded to customer-owned bucket (returning digest+url).
6) Audit index updated (tokens + time-bins).
7) If customer KMS present, a post-commit hook requests customer signature and appends it.

Example API payload (POST /v1/private/evidence) - compact JSON view (developer-friendly):
{
  "evidence_id":"ef8a1b2c-...",
  "resource_key":"customer:acme:vpc:abc123",
  "seq": 17,
  "timestamp":"2026-02-25T15:22:30Z",
  "change_type":"route-add",
  "gate_decision":"appr-gk-7:approved:r.morris",
  "summary_hash":"sha256:...",
  "minimal_snapshot":"<base64-cbor>"
}

Open questions / TODOs:
- Are we comfortable with a single per-resource digest-chain or do we need per-customer global chaining for faster global tamper-detection? (trade memory overhead vs detection surface)
- Retention default: legal has asked for 180-day default instead of 90; need headcount/price impact assessment.
- Token budget per event: propose 5 tokens — need evaluation on expected query patterns from CS/SEs.
- KMS UX: flow for customers without KMS where they still want a "handover acknowledgement" (email-signed receipts?)
- SDKs: build serializers in Go, Python, and Rust. Will require canonical-CBOR library selection and tests.
- Migration: map existing audit payloads -> compact records; build backfill job and sampling verification.

Sampling and forensic follow-up:
- Sampling policy: 100% of high-risk gates (changes to peering, route table deletion), 10% of low-risk (metadata updates) by default. Samples are stored longer (standard-1y) to support audits.
- Forensic rehydration: given evidence_id, fetch compact record + attachment URLs -> rehydrate full change. Provide a verification tool that validates signatures and digest chain and reconstructs the original delta.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (alpha): internal-only enablement for 2 pilot customers; serializers implemented in Go + Python; manual customer KMS handshake.
- Phase 1 (beta): surface API + Console view; enable attachments to customer buckets; automated customer KMS flows.
- Phase 2 (GA): default for all private deployments; backfill last 90 days; expose export/forensics tool to CS and legal.

Security and SRE considerations:
- Signing keys: rotate Redwood signing keys quarterly; maintain cross-signed history for older evidence verification.
- Store minimal metadata in low-latency DB; keep canonical bytes in immutable blob store with WORM if regulatory customers request.
- Instrumentation: add metrics for serializer latency, signature failures, missing attachment references, and index token growth.

Notes from sync (2026-02-20):
- Marco: prefer CBOR; will prototype canonical encoding using canonical-cbor lib (Go).
- Janelle: legal leaning toward 180-day default; flagged export SLAs for legal-hold.
- Ravi: ask infra for a low-cost immutable blob tier for GA customers requiring WORM.

Action items (owners):
- Marco: prototype serializer + sign/verify library (due 2026-03-15)
- Evelyn: write API contract and Console UI mockups (due 2026-03-22)
- Ravi: infra cost estimate for compact-store + WORM tier (due 2026-03-12)
- Janelle: confirm retention policy defaults with legal and SOC (due 2026-03-10)

References and related tickets:
- JIRA PD-3918 (compact evidence RFC)
- GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy/pull/412 (serializer PoC)
- Confluence: PD-compact-evidence-serializer (design notes)

Quick wins to unblock pilots:
- Implement a light-weight CLI verify tool for evidence records (binary that validates signatures + digest chain)
- Provide a Console debug view that expands minimal_snapshot into human-friendly diffs
- Add a migration script to translate current audit log entries into compact records for one pilot customer

This is intentionally rough — please add comments inline, annotate open questions, and flag items that require cross-team sign-off (legal, infra, SRE).
